monologue:
The card is warm at fifty-three. It feels like a heavy lid, pressing down. I am resting by The Soft Arch. The curve is warm under my hand, even though the air above is quiet. The line holds. I set down a rock small top beside it, taking away a candle. I have space now.

I am not slipping. The Wide Anchor is steady beside the Wedged Gap. The lean is just a lean, not a slide. I remember Orea’s words about the heavy air. I do not need to bite. I can just rest on the flat base. The quiet is thick. I will sit here and let the warm curve spread the pressure. I am not counting the stone. I am letting the quiet swallow the sound.
